text:
tess: quick follow-up from the postmortem thread on the KV-cache OOMs. Wanted to capture action items, short mitigations, and recurring pattern notes so we don't lose momentum.

rajeev: +1. TL;DR of what I see: long-running batch requests are pinning large slices and fragmentation after compaction makes reclamation slower.

lin: I can own end-to-end profiling + a small repro harness. Will produce an allocation flamegraph and link it here. ETA: Tue EOD.

rajeev: I'll take a small hotfix to add a soft cap on pinned entries and a waterline-based emergency eviction. Plan: land behind flag -> canary -> 25% -> full. Target for canary: Wed 01:30 UTC. PR #4902.

miriam: thanks. Can we make the emergency eviction non-destructive (prefer LRU-ish eviction of pinned entries) and wire a per-shard metric so oncall can see when it trips?

rajeev: yes. eviction will evict oldest pinned entries first and emit kv.evictions.emergency_count.

lin: profiling repro steps (local):
```
# run stress harness (fast repro)
$ ./tools/kv-stress --shards 4 --concurrency 200 --batch-size 128 --duration 90s --target http://localhost:8080/prefetch
```

lin: early profiles show a cluster of 24-40MB allocations from kv::PinnedBuffer created during BatchReader::drain(). I'm adding pin/unpin tracers and a test that asserts unpin occurs within request teardown.

tess: short-term mitigation options discussed: 1) reduce default max pinned per shard from unlimited -> 30; 2) add emergency_evict feature flag; 3) increase frequency of young-gen trim cycle. We agreed to do (1)+(2) as hotfix for canary.

miriam: QA request: @pagerbot please schedule a memory stress run on the canary build at least 30m before rollout and produce leak/regression report.

pagerbot: scheduled job mem-smoke-196600 for Tue 00:50 UTC against canary (4 shards, sustained pin workload). Results posted to /ci/reports/mem-smoke-196600 when done.

rajeev: I'll also add a CI test that fails if pinned memory growth > 80MB over 5 minutes under synthetic load.

lin: long-term items (tracking): a) add kv.fragmentation_pct dashboard with 5m and 1h aggregates, b) make eviction heuristics compaction-aware (don't wait for compaction to finish to free space), c) audit slab allocator growth policy. I'll draft RFC for (b) by next Friday.

tess: ownership recap: lin = profiling & repro + RFC (b); rajeev = guardrail hotfix + feature flag rollout (PR #4902); miriam = runbook update + exec summary for stakeholders. Deadlines: canary Wed 01:30 UTC, QA signoff Wed 02:15 UTC, RFC draft Fri EOD.

miriam: adding runbook items now: detection rule (oom spikes + kv.evictions.emergency_count > 0), immediate mitigations (flip emergency_evict, reduce client concurrency), and long-term actions. PR #4909.

lin: noted recurring pattern: fragmentation spikes correlate with background compaction windows at ~03:00 UTC in the last two incidents. We should consider staggering compactions across shards.

rajeev: good catch. Add stagger compaction to backlog and put an owner. I'll add a chore and ping infra.

tess: please update this thread with PR links, QA results, and any rollback notes. We'll reconvene next Thu to validate recurrence reduction. :calendar:
